_comment: Default mock for Claire's ticket. Two distinct touchpoints: (1) aiCall = the AI agent (Lily / Survey Health Voice) biweekly wellness check that flagged this ticket — drives the call recording + transcript + extracted responses card at the TOP of the page. (2) nurseCall = the human follow-up call by Lisa Goldenstein, RN — drives the AI Summary card with the 13-field CCM note at the BOTTOM. Live Quo + LLM output overrides nurseCall when 'Listen for AI call' captures a fresh call.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi, this is Lily, calling on behalf of Everyday Health Clinic. Is this Claire?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: This is.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you have about a minute for your biweekly health check?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you. Please answer the following in your own words. In the past week, have you had any increased shortness of breath and/or hacking cough that limits your normal activities?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I do. I've been coughing up a lot more, and it doesn't look good at all.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I understand. In the past week, have you been taking your medications like your doctor ordered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm not sure if I'm taking the right doses or the right medications. I'm a little confused on that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for letting me know. In the past week, have you felt like you needed medical help, even if you didn't end up asking for help?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yeah. I — I think there was one time where I think I really did need help. I was too much of a hassle. I didn't wanna go to emergency room, but maybe I should have.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me a little more about what's been worse?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: You know, I'm just coughing up a lot more, and it doesn't look great. And I'm, you know, a little bit short of breath when I do activities.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it. Compared to last month, is your general wellness better, worse or the same?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Well, to include last week, it's worse. I mean, I'm not feeling better. So, yeah, I need to be seen.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: In the past month, have you experienced any new or unbearable symptoms that limit your normal activities, such as pain, fever, nausea, diarrhea, or vomiting?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: None of those. I mean, I did — you a little zebraish, but it, it's mainly the my shortness of breath that's bothering me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for sharing that. It sounds like you need to be seen by your care team. We'll now send you a text message so you can take your vital signs on your phone. Please look for the message and follow the instructions when it arrives.

callMeta.agentName: Lisa Goldenstein, RN — Survey Health Care Manager

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi Claire, this is Lisa from Survey Health calling on behalf of Everyday Health Clinic. Is now still a good time to talk for a couple of minutes?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, yes, it is. Thanks for calling back so quickly.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Of course. I'm following up on the wellness check you did earlier this morning. You mentioned more shortness of breath and a cough that's been bothering you — is that still going on?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It is. I've been coughing up a lot more, and honestly it doesn't look good. Even getting up the stairs is hard now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay, thank you for telling me. And how about your medications — are you confident you're taking the right doses?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Not really. I'm a little confused on which one is which. My daughter usually helps but she's been away.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's helpful for me to know. Have you felt at any point this week that you needed to be seen — even if you didn't end up calling anyone?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes. There was one night I almost called, but I didn't want to be a hassle. Maybe I should have.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're not a hassle, Claire. That's exactly what we're here for. Compared to last month, would you say you're feeling better, worse, or about the same?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Worse. Definitely worse. I'm not getting better, and I think I need to be seen.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay. Any new pain, fever, nausea, vomiting — anything else that's new this past month?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, none of that. It's mainly the breathing and the cough.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it. Here's what I'd like to do. I'm going to get you on the schedule today or tomorrow with Dr. Henderson's team — I think you should be seen sooner rather than later. In the meantime, please continue your furosemide in the morning and the lisinopril as prescribed.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, I can do that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: And one more thing — I'm going to send you a quick text so you can take your blood pressure and weight on your phone. It only takes about a minute and helps the team see what's happening before your visit.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Alright, I'll watch for it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Before I let you go, let's quickly go over your medications so I can make sure you're on the right ones. Can you grab your pill bottles?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hold on, let me get them. Okay, I have furosemide, lisinopril, and a multivitamin.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great. Furosemide is the water pill — once in the morning. Lisinopril is for blood pressure — once a day. Are you taking those at the same time every day?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I try to but some days I forget the morning one.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay. I'll have your nurse set up a pill organizer when she calls back, and we'll have your daughter help when she's back in town. If anything gets worse before we talk again — chest pain, severe shortness of breath at rest, or you feel lightheaded — please call 911 right away. I'll be in touch within the next two hours with your appointment time. Take care, Claire.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, Lisa.

note.goals: No ED visits and no hospitalizations this calendar year.
note.evaluationReason: Follow-up to flagged AI biweekly wellness check earlier this morning — patient reported worsening dyspnea, increased cough, medication confusion, and a self-identified need for clinical attention.
note.summaryOfInteraction: Spoke with Ms. Henderson by phone for 4 minutes and 18 seconds. Patient reports progressive shortness of breath when climbing stairs over the past 7–9 days, an increase in cough volume and productivity, mild bilateral ankle swelling in the evenings, and a 3-lb weight gain from last week. New orthopnea — needing to prop up on pillows overnight. Denies chest pain, palpitations, fever, nausea, or vomiting. Medication reconciliation completed on call — patient confirmed furosemide AM, lisinopril daily, and a multivitamin; reports occasionally missing the morning dose, with usual support from daughter currently unavailable. Patient expressed she felt she should have been seen earlier in the week. Compared to last month, patient reports her general wellness is worse and explicitly stated she needs to be seen.
note.plan:
1. Schedule same-day or next-day visit with Dr. Henderson's team; nurse to confirm appointment within 2 hours.
2. Reconcile medications on next call — confirm furosemide AM dose and lisinopril; offer pill-organizer setup with daughter when she returns.
3. Send RPM prompt for BP and weight reading; alert threshold +2 lb/day or +5 lb/week.
4. Reinforce 2 g sodium diet and fluid guidance; reviewed CHF decompensation warning signs with patient.
5. Patient instructed to call 911 if chest pain, severe SOB at rest, or lightheadedness develops before her visit.
6. Flag ticket as Evaluation — High priority pending PCP review.

summary.oneLine: Likely early CHF decompensation — worsening dyspnea, productive cough, new orthopnea, 3-lb weight gain, and medication confusion. Same-day clinic visit being arranged.
